title: Sussex racecourse named one of the UK's most haunted after 147 paranormal reports
excerpt: Brighton has been named the second most haunted racecourse in UK.
content:
Brighton named second most haunted racecourse in the UK

Brighton Racecourse. (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald.

Brighton has been named the second most haunted racecourse in the UK.

With Halloween approaching, a new ranking by AskGamblers placed Brighton Racecourse as the second most haunted of 60 courses.

The Paranormal Database lists 147 reports for Brighton, more than any other racecourse town in the country.

The track is also just 0.07 miles from the City Cemetery.

Racing has been held on the current site since 1783.

Only Chester, which scored 8.27 out of 10, ranks higher than Brighton, which achieved a score of 8.13.

Brighton is the highest-ranked course in Sussex, significantly ahead of Plumpton, Goodwood and Fontwell Park.

The study looked at three factors to determine a racecourse's haunted score: the distance from the track to the nearest cemetery or churchyard, how long racing has been recorded there and the number of paranormal reports listed for its town.

Courses with a documented ghost or curse story of their own, such as Chester's grandstand ghosts, earned a bonus point.

The haunted score was then calculated as the average of the three factors plus any bonus, capped at 10.

The research also found that 42 of the 60 racing tracks are within half a mile of a cemetery or churchyard and 56 are within a mile.
